verdict.reasoning: Patient reports 'aching all over' and 'feeling really tired, run down' and doctor notes 'symptoms, which have been ongoing for six weeks'.
Patient states symptoms started 'probably a couple of weeks after I got back' from a holiday in the States that was 'End of January, start of Feb.'

Decreased energy: 'yeah, less energy...'; mild headaches: 'it's the sort of headache maybe in just generally feeling a bit crappy'; decreased appetite/smaller portions: 'probably less hungry' and 'slightly smaller portions'; transient calf rash: 'back of my calf… around the end of February… faded over a couple of weeks'; arthralgia shoulders/back/hips/knees: 'sort of aching shoulders, back, the hips, knees'.

Denies URTI/cough/SOB: 'Uh, no' to chest/cough/shortness of breath; denies abdominal/GI: 'No' to abdominal pain and 'Uh, no' to change in bowel habit/diarrhoea/vomiting/blood; denies GU: 'No, that's all fine'; denies current rash: 'I don't have any rashes now'; denies neurological deficits: 'Um, no' to headaches, blurred vision, tingling, numbness. Weight change: 'no weight change'.
Patient states: 'Asthma and hay fever if they can help.'

Preventer inhaler: 'I've got one of those, um, preventative... I've been using the everyday for the morning and night'; OTC antihistamine: 'I take, um, one of the antihistamines... I get that from, just from the pharmacy.'
Work: 'I work for a health technology company actually.' Lives with wife: 'just my wife.'
Alcohol: Patient clarifies 'occasionally' after doctor asks 'Drink any alcohol?'

Patient shows a photo: 'I've got a photo, um, on my phone... you see that?' Doctor responds 'OK, right, yeah'; rash location and resolution described: 'back of my calf... it faded over a couple of weeks.' This supports a reviewed, now-resolved erythematous-looking calf rash.
'Aching all over' and 'feeling really tired, run down' for 'the last six weeks' with no diagnosis yet; doctor says 'we would need to investigate... cause reduced energy, tiredness and aching'.

Doctor states: 'you can get... lyme disease that you can get a rash like that from a tick bite. So that's something we would do a test for' after systemic symptoms and rash post-travel, indicating Lyme as a possible diagnosis.

Doctor: 'get some blood tests, checking all the normal things, like liver, kidneys, blood count, etc. But also… a bacterial infection… called lyme disease that you can get a rash like that from a tick bite. So that would involve blood tests.' This supports FBC (blood count), U&E (kidneys), LFT (liver), and Lyme serology as part of a fatigue workup.
Doctor: 'when you've had the test arrange a follow up about a week after, after you've had the test done… we can do that over the phone to start with.'
Doctor: 'if that comes back positive, then there are specific antibiotics that we would give you to treat it' referring to Lyme disease testing.
